function.name: sb_list_projects
function.description: The project this token is scoped to (one token = one project), your role in it, and counts of documents, entity pages, canon facts, pending candidates, open conflicts and open tasks. Call first to confirm what you are connected to. Example: {}

function.name: sb_get_context_pack
function.description: Compact briefing on an entity (character, place, faction, rule) or topic: the accepted canon facts about it, each with verbatim source quotes and document ids/lines, plus open conflicts touching them. Use before writing or editing lore. Returns status "unknown" when canon has nothing. Example: {"topic": "Odo", "limit": 15}

topic.description: Entity name or topic, e.g. "Mara Venn" or "tide bell rules"

function.name: sb_search_facts
function.description: Keyword search over accepted canon facts (statement, subject, object). Returns compact hits with ids; use sb_get_fact for full evidence. Empty result means canon has nothing on it ("unknown"), not that it is false. Example: {"query": "Ashbell voice", "limit": 10}

function.name: sb_get_fact
function.description: One fact by id with status and all its evidence (verbatim quote, document id, file, line range). Accepted canon only; pending, rejected and superseded facts are refused (NOT_CANON). Example: {"fact_id": "fact_0123abcd4567ef89"}

function.name: sb_list_documents
function.description: The imported source documents (scenes, lore, dialogue…) at their latest version: id, title, file name, folder, kind, tags, version, how many canon facts cite it and how many of those need a re-check after a newer version. Paginated. Filters combine. Example: {"kind": "scene", "folder": "Act 1", "limit": 20}

folder.description: Folder name or path, e.g. "Act 1" or "Act 1 / Scenes" (case-insensitive; a folder includes its subfolders)

query.description: Words in the title or file name

needs_recheck.description: Only documents with canon citations to re-check

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page

function.name: sb_read_document
function.description: Source text of one document, passage by passage (a passage is a paragraph or heading), with line numbers and the canon facts citing each passage. Latest version unless you pass version. Narrow with a line range or passage ids; long results are paged (next_cursor) and capped by max_chars; a passage longer than max_chars comes in parts (part.from_char/to_char), join them before quoting. Copy quotes for sb_propose_candidate from here, character for character. Example: {"document": "S03-the-kettle-and-coal.md", "from_line": 1, "to_line": 40}

document.description: Document id (any version) or file name

version.description: A specific version; default: the latest (or the version the id names)

passage_ids.description: Only these passages (ids from evidence or a previous read)

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page

function.name: sb_list_entities
function.description: The project's wiki pages (characters, locations, items, factions, events and any types the team made): id, name, type, aliases and how many canon facts name it. The summary is editorial (not canon). Paginated. Example: {"type": "character", "query": "odo"}

type.description: Entity type key, e.g. "character", "location"; the result lists the project's types

query.description: Words in a name or alias

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page

function.name: sb_get_entity
function.description: Everything about one entity page: canon facts naming it (with quotes and sources), its relationships and timeline from canon, open conflicts touching it, pending candidates, where it appears in the sources, and the team's editorial wiki text (summary, aliases, typed fields, notes) clearly marked not canon. canon.status is "unknown" when no accepted fact names it. Example: {"entity": "Odo"}

facts_limit.description: Max canon facts with full evidence

function.name: sb_get_timeline
function.description: Accepted canon facts with a story time, in story order: what happens when, with a source for each. Filter by a time window and/or an entity. Story time "D<day> HH:MM" or day-only "D<day>" (the whole day); the day may be 0 or negative for before D1, e.g. "D2 14:30", "D-3650". A day-only time ("D5") means some time that day; "~" marks approximate times; negative days are before the story starts. Paginated. Example: {"entity": "Odo", "from": "D1", "to": "D2 23:59"}

to.description: Window end, e.g. "D3 12:00"; a day-only end covers that whole day

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page

function.name: sb_ask
function.description: A question answered from accepted canon only, the same as Ask in the web app: the answer (when a live model is configured) plus the canon facts it rests on, each with quotes. status: "supported" (answer + citations), "source_only" (the matching facts, no prose answer: recorded mode or model offline) or "unknown" (canon has nothing; do not guess). Example: {"question": "Who rang the Ashbell before the story starts?"}

function.name: sb_check_facts
function.description: Dry-run continuity check: pass the facts a scene or draft would add and get the rule-based conflicts they would raise against accepted canon, and among themselves. Nothing is stored. Deterministic, no model. Rules: EXACT/APPROX_TIME_LOCATION_OVERLAP (same subject, predicate "located_at", object = the place, overlapping clock times), TRAVEL_TIME_TOO_SHORT (two located_at facts closer than a canon "travel_time" fact allows; travel_time: subject and object are the two places, value = minutes), RELATIONSHIP_AFTER_END (kind "relationship", same predicate and object, used after a canon relationship ended at time_to). Day-only times never clash on place. World-rule checks need a model and are not run. No hits is not proof of consistency. Story time "D<day> HH:MM" or day-only "D<day>" (the whole day); the day may be 0 or negative for before D1, e.g. "D2 14:30", "D-3650". Example: {"facts": [{"kind": "event", "subject": "Odo", "predicate": "located_at", "object": "Saltgate", "time_from": "D1 21:00", "time_to": "D1 22:00"}]}

time_precision.description: Default exact when a time is given

statement.description: The fact as a sentence, echoed back

function.name: sb_list_conflicts
function.description: Possible canon conflicts found by the rule checks (time/place overlap, travel time, relationship after end, world-rule violations). These are candidates for a human to judge, not verdicts. Default: open ones. Paginated. Example: {"status": "open"}

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page

function.name: sb_get_impact
function.description: What a change would touch: accepted facts and scenes within max 2 hops of a canon fact (fact_id), or the stored impact of an existing change proposal (change_id). Pass exactly one. Each item has path, evidence ids and rationale. An empty list means "no impact found within accepted canon, max 2 hops", not a guarantee of none. Example: {"fact_id": "fact_0123abcd4567ef89"}

function.name: sb_list_recheck
function.description: Canon facts whose citation points at an older version of its source after a new version was imported. "outdated": the quoted words are gone from the latest version (or appear more than once), a person must decide; "unchanged": the words still read the same, a person only confirms. Read-only: re-pinning is done by a person in the web app. Paginated. Example: {"state": "outdated"}

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page

function.name: sb_list_tasks
function.description: Re-review tasks: one per scene in an applied change's impact, with the passage to re-read, the change that caused it, the dependency path and who it is assigned to. Default: active (open and in progress). Read-only. Paginated. Example: {"status": "active"}

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; omit for the first page

function.name: sb_propose_candidate
function.description: Propose a NEW fact for human review. It becomes a pending candidate in the review queue, marked as proposed by this agent; it is NOT canon until a person accepts it. The quote must appear verbatim in one passage (paragraph) of the latest version of an imported document, or the proposal is refused and nothing is stored; curly vs straight quotes, dash style, line breaks and Markdown * _ marks may differ, and the source's exact characters are stored. Requires editor role or above. Example: {"document": "S03-the-kettle-and-coal.md", "quote": "<exact words from sb_read_document>", "statement": "Odo keeps the inn's ledger.", "kind": "claim", "subject": "Odo", "predicate": "keeps", "object": "the inn's ledger"}

document.description: Imported document id, or its file name when only one document has that name. The latest version is cited.

quote.description: Exact text copied from the document

statement.description: The fact as one plain sentence

time_from.description: Story time "D<day> HH:MM" or day-only "D<day>" (the whole day); the day may be 0 or negative for before D1, e.g. "D2 14:30", "D-3650"

message.content: That initial search came up empty, so I'll check the timeline and entity records directly.
